evidence: Judge: task.toml:30-35 [verifier.env] REWARDKIT_JUDGE="claude-code", REWARDKIT_MODEL="z-ai/glm-5.3-flashx" via OpenRouter, byte-identical to template (diff of task.toml shows only [task]/[metadata] lines). All five judge.toml files carry only the expected fallback judge="claude-code" with no model/effort/temperature, so one shared agent+model grades every dimension. CLIs/browser: tests/Dockerfile is byte-identical to the template (diff empty) and pins @anthropic-ai/claude-code@2.1.281, @openai/codex@0.151.0, @playwright/mcp@0.0.79, harbor-rewardkit==0.1.7 (lines 16-31); Chromium is installed through the mcp package's own Playwright CLI (lines 33-38), and every judge.toml launches playwright-mcp with --executable-path=/usr/local/bin/chromium. Runtime check in local image qc-r22-kittle-verifier:r1 (its /tests/test.sh, tools/score.py, tools/restart_mcp.py sha256 bd682592..., 13de2b38..., 03c1426f... equal the frozen files): claude 2.1.281, rewardkit 0.1.7, codex-cli 0.151.0, @playwright/mcp 0.0.79 depending on exact playwright 1.63.0-alpha-2026-08-05, browsers chromium-1237, /usr/local/bin/chromium = Chrome for Testing 152.0.7977.8. rewardkit agents.py ensure_installed only installs when the CLI is absent, so the pinned CLI is used, not a fresh latest install. Shared tools test.sh/score.py/restart_mcp.py are byte-identical to template. Order determinism: functional mode="individual" with rewardkit --max-concurrent-agent 1 (test.sh:207); rewardkit judges.py _arun_agent_individual iterates criteria sequentially in listed order, so the cross-criterion state dependencies (e.g. deleted_message_takes_its_versions after timer_changes, persistence last) run in a fixed order. Fixed clock: kittle.json:2 "clock": "2026-05-12T11:00:00Z" (environment/assets and solution seed identical, cmp); public brief integration.md:7 and walls-and-retention.md:23 state timers are measured against that clock; app_context.md:27 tells the judge the clock is fixed; graded boundary data are stored times (Boundary note at 2026-05-05T11:00:00Z, control at 11:00:01Z, original lease scan 2026-05-01, Insurer letter 2026-05-03, Probate 2026-05-04), and the golden computes expiry as CLOCK_MS - Date.parse(r.at) (server.js:33,143) with new messages stamped CLOCK (server.js:409,430). The scripted golden ran on 8 Oct 2026, five months after the fixed date, and golden-run.log:8-10 shows deleted_parent_placeholder, timer_boundary and timer_changes PASS, i.e. the graded time rules do not depend on the run date. No criterion compares against the judge's real date. Adversarial: a broken app that uses Date.now() would, on any real run date, delete the one-second-younger control "Rent review meeting moved to the afternoon." and fail deleted_and_expired_seed_messages Part B, so it cannot pass by luck of the date; a conforming app that reads the brief's fixed clock passes regardless of run date and any time format is accepted (app_context.md:27). Network is public by delivery profile, not a defect. Residual notes (not defects for this row, template-controlled, no observed impact): base images node:22-bookworm-slim/python:3.12-slim are tag- not digest-pinned and apt fonts are unpinned; provider-side model behaviour behind the OpenRouter id is outside task control. No full configured judge run exists, but this row's pinning/clock claims are established by source, image inspection and the scripted golden; full-judge evidence is the subject of other rows.
